==English== {{phrasebook|en|Greetings}} {{was wotd|2007|November|19}} {{wp}} ===Alternative forms=== * {{alt|en|hullo||UK}} * {{alt|en|hallo|hollo||UK|dated}} * {{alt|en|hilloa||obsolete}} ===Etymology=== {{etydate|1826}}. From {{m|en|holla}}, {{m|en|hollo}} (attested 1588). This variant of {{m|en|hallo}} is often credited to {{w|Thomas Edison}} as a coinage for telephone use, but its appearance in print predates the invention of the telephone by several decades. Ultimately from a variant of {{der|en|ang|ēalā}}, such as {{m|ang|hēlā}}, which was used colloquially at the time similarly to how ''hey'' and (in some dialects) ''hi'' are used nowadays. Thus, equivalent to a compound of {{m|en|hey}} and {{m|en|lo}}. Used when drawing attention to yourself. Possibly influenced by {{ncog|osx|halo}}, {{lg|imperative}} of {{m|osx|halōn|t=to call, fetch}}, used in hailing a ferryman, akin to {{cog|goh|hala}}, {{m|goh|hola|hola!}}, imperative forms of {{m|goh|halōn}}, {{m|goh|holōn|t=to fetch}}. For more information, see {{l|en|hallo}}. The ''{{w|Oxford English Dictionary}}'' and ''{{w|Merriam-Webster Dictionary}}'' also suggested that it is a variant of {{m|en|holla}}, a variant of {{m|en|holloo}}. Further beyond, the origin remains uncertain. OED and Merriam-Webster suggested that it has a connection between {{m|en|hallow|t=to shout, to cry out loud}}, which came from Old French {{m|fro|holloer}}, which, according to ''Altfranzösisches Wörterbuch'', is from {{cog|osx|halōn}}. ===Pronunciation=== * {{enPR|hĕ-lō'|hə-lō'}} ** {{IPA|en|/hɛˈloʊ/|/hə-/|/ˈhɛloʊ/|a=GA}} ** {{a|en|UK}} *** {{IPA|en|/həˈləʊ/|/hɛ-/|a=RP}} **** {{audio|en|En-uk-hello.ogg|a=UK}} *** {{IPA|en|/haˈlaʊ/|a=Northumbrian}} ** {{IPA|en|/həˈləʉ/|a=AU}} *** {{audio|en|En-au-hello.ogg|a=AU}} ** {{IPA|en|/hɛˈloː/|/hə-/|/ˈhɛlo(ː)/|a=CA}} ** {{IPA|en|/həˈlo(w)/|a=Indic}} * {{rhymes|en|ɛləʊ|əʊ|s=2}} * {{hmp|en|hallow}} {| class="wikitable" ! Is anyone there?}} #* {{RQ:Lincoln Pratt's Patients|chapter=7|passage=I made a speaking trumpet of my hands and commenced to whoop “Ahoy!” and “'''Hello!'''” at the top of my lungs. {{...}} The Colonel woke up, and, after asking what in brimstone was the matter, opened his mouth and roared “Hi!” and “'''Hello!'''” like the bull of Bashan.}} # {{lb|en|colloquial}} {{n-g|Used [[sarcastic]]ally to imply that the person addressed has done something the speaker considers to be [[foolish]], or missed something that should have been [[obvious]].}} #: {{ux|en|You just tried to start your car with your cell phone. '''Hello'''?}} #* {{quote-av|en|year=1995|writer=w:Amy Heckerling|title=w:Clueless|actor=w:Stacey Dash|actor2=w:Alicia Silverstone|role=w:Dionne Davenport|role2=w:Cher Horowitz |passage=Dionne: '''Hello'''? There was a stop sign.
Cher: I totally paused.}} #* {{quote-video game|en|year=2004|tlr=w:Nintendo of America|title=w:Paper Mario: The Thousand-Year Door|developer=Intelligent Systems|publisher=w:Nintendo|system=w:GameCube|level=Rogueport |text=Uh, '''hello'''? We're using a CANNON to get to the moon? Isn't that, like, dangerous?}} # {{lb|en|chiefly|UK}} {{n-g|An expression of [[puzzlement]] or [[discovery]].}} #: {{syn|en|Thesaurus:wow}} #: {{ux|en|'''Hello'''! What’s going on here?}} ====Usage notes==== The greeting {{m|en|hello}} is among the most universal and neutral in use. It may be heard in nearly all social situations and nearly all walks of life and is unlikely to offend. In the derived senses, the word-final stress may be emphasized to focus attention, but word-initial stress is also heard in certain contexts, such as some uses of {{m|en|hello there}}, and even in isolation. ====Derived terms==== {{col|en |golden hello |hello again|say hello to my little friend |hello girl |helloji |hello nurse |hello there |Hello World |hello yourself, and see how you like it
